_why: Single source for the protocol's text budgets. scripts/anet_payload.sh reads this file; SKILL.md's
budget table must carry the same numbers, and the eval criterion
budgets-in-docs-match-the-script refuses a drift between them.
Budgets are CHARACTERS (hub limits and the 200-char preview are character-counted too). Chinese is
not cheaper: it costs about 1 token per character, and on the Dashboard's Latin-width UI a CJK
character renders full-width. Use `guard`'s cjk_share/est_tokens line to self-assess.

task_max 800 (operator order 2026-11-09): the pointer budget is now wide enough to carry an item-by-item acceptance list, so a pointer body still points at a payload file (`file:` + `sha12:`) — the payload-file route is NOT replaced by the wider parameter, and the sha12 stays the proof of which revision the worker works on. Cost recorded, not hidden: the pointer enters the worker's context on every dispatch (800 characters ≈ 800 tokens, CJK ≈ 1 token/character), and the Dashboard's node card shows only a blind 200-character slice, so line 3+ is invisible there.

2026-11-09 (operator design note): a dispatch body is a formatted summary, not a wall of text — markdown from line 2 on, the detail in the payload file. task_lines_max is therefore 0 (no line cap) and markup is graded by line: line 1 plain, line 2+ markdown, tables refused everywhere.

measured.pointer_body_headroom_at_480: 480 - 271 = 209 spare chars; raised to 800 (2026-11-09, operator order) so a pointer can carry the whole requirement list inline while the steps stay in the payload file: 800 - 271 = 529 spare

hard_constraints.result_first_340_chars: line 1 = the conclusion, lines 2-12 (the 300px the task pane shows before '展开全文 ⌄') = the evidence; the item-by-item acceptance list goes after them, and the long report goes in the payload file
hard_constraints.ttl_rule: ttl_seconds >= 2 * node idle budget (checked by compose --ttl/--node-idle; the hub does not check it: default 3600, max 86400)

markdown_policy.line1: plain text only, self-sufficient, <= line1_max characters: it is all the previews show
markdown_policy.line2_plus: markdown allowed (# headings, **bold**, '- ' bullets, '1.' numbering, > quotes, inline code) — the task pane renders it (react-markdown + remark-gfm)
markdown_policy.cost: the Tasks detail page and Messages render plain text, so from line 2 the markup shows as its own characters there; that is the accepted price of a formatted dispatch body
